label: review-00-reader
scope_note: Fresh review of the edited chapter; replaces the pre-edit review. Ran sync 00 (written=0 unchanged=3). Read 1-fast.md, calendar.md, mistakes.md, sources.md, data/plan.json and data/00-start-here/tasks.json (items []). The edit closed the old W307, W105 and W901 findings: the ESL displays are now links, minutes.full is 25, 'resilient' and 'stem' are bold and explained. calendar-preview.md was no longer in 00-start-here/ when this review ran (removed 09:46 local), although the orchestrator note said to leave it for finalize; the brief (brief.json lines 250 to 323) was used for the preview's intent. Skim test: headings, bold text and tables give a mostly correct gist, with three exceptions: the bold step 'Then book Day 19 of Plan A' without a deadline check (r00-01), the Plan B table that jumps from Day 1 to Day 15 (r00-11) and the Gate 2 rows (r00-10, r00-32). Recaps 1 and 2 need the body text; Recap 3 is answerable from the moves table alone (r00-21). Depth: a front chapter teaches no service; the one transferable exam skill it teaches (find the constraint in the stem) lacks its cause (r00-15). Line numbers are those of the files on 2026-10-12 after the edit.

findings.quote: 2. **Then book Day 19 of Plan A.** Choose a [Pearson VUE](../facts/exam.md#exam-testing-options) test center or online proctoring.
findings.evidence: Facts exam-results-timing ("Final results will be posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the close of the exam.") and exam-retake-wait ("If you fail an exam, you must wait 14 calendar days before you are eligible to retake the exam."). READER.md line 7: pass by Oct 31, 2026. Today is Monday 2026-10-12. If Day 1 is Oct 13, Day 19 is Saturday Oct 31 and the result can come as late as Nov 6; any later Day 1 puts Day 19 itself past the deadline. calendar.md applies the five-business-day check only to Plan B (line 91: 'Count five business days from Day 23: if that passes your deadline, Plan B does not fit'), never to Plan A, and 1-fast.md never mentions a deadline. The step is bold, so it is the gist of a skim, and she 'acts before she reads' (READER.md). Fix: 'Count 19 days from your Day 1. If Day 19 plus five business days passes your deadline, read Plan C in calendar.md first.' and the same check after the Plan A table.
findings.resolution: 1-fast.md step 3 is now 'Then choose a plan in calendar.md, check your deadline, and book.'; calendar.md how-to-use-this-calendar has the five-business-day deadline check for every plan.

findings.quote: 3. **Take the free official practice set.** The free Official Practice Question Sets on AWS Skill Builder are [20-question sets](../facts/exam.md#exam-official-practice-question-sets). Take the SAA-C03 set first, as your baseline.
findings.evidence: data/plan.json g4: 'Plan choice. Choose Plan C only if your official practice set is 70% or more ... Otherwise follow Plan A.' The set that decides the plan comes after step 2 books Plan A, so choosing Plan C spends one reschedule (fact exam-reschedule-limit: "Each exam appointment can only be rescheduled twice.") and the Plan C fallback to Day 19 spends the second, which leaves none for Gate 1 or Gate 2 (calendar.md line 148: 'Each plan switch uses one of the two.'). calendar.md Day 1 lists ESL and the practice set but no booking task, so the two files give different Day 1 orders. 'Take the SAA-C03 set first' in step 3 also contradicts the numbering and hints at other sets that are never named. Fix: ESL, then the practice set, then choose the plan, then book.
findings.resolution: Order is now ESL, practice set, choose the plan, book (1-fast.md and plan.json d01 of all three plans); 'Take the SAA-C03 set first' replaced.

findings.quote: 2. **Then book Day 19 of Plan A.**
findings.evidence: 1-fast.md never names or links calendar.md, where Plan A, Day 19 and the gates are defined; 'Plan A' appears here for the first time with no explanation. The file list under 'How a chapter works' (lines 62 to 67) shows the files of a service chapter, not the files of this chapter (calendar.md, mistakes.md), so the folder she opens does not match the list she just read. READER.md: 'Put the short version first, always' and she acts on one glance. Fix: one line in 'What you get': 'This chapter has three files: this one, `calendar.md` (Plans A, B and C) and `mistakes.md` (your log).' and link calendar.md in step 2.
findings.resolution: Step 3 names calendar.md. The three-files sentence was drafted but cut for the 800-word file limit (L201); the step link gives the route to the calendar.

findings.quote: Choose it only if your Day 1 practice set is 70% or more and a recorded fail costs you nothing. <!-- no-fact: plan -->
findings.evidence: Same file line 125: 'You also pay the [full registration fee for each exam attempt](../facts/exam.md#exam-retake-attempts-and-fee), [150 USD](../facts/exam.md#exam-cost) for this exam.' (fact exam-retake-attempts-and-fee: "However, you must pay the full registration fee for each exam attempt."). Read literally, a fail always costs 150 USD and 14 days, so the condition can never be true. The intended meaning (a fail has no consequence for your job or your record) is an idiom for a second-language reader (STYLE.md line 61), and 'recorded' suggests an AWS record that the chapter never grounds. Fix: 'and you accept the cost of a second attempt: 150 USD and 14 days.'
findings.resolution: The idiom 'a recorded fail costs you nothing' is removed from calendar.md and plan.json (note, g4); it now says accept the cost of a fail, with the 14-day wait and full fee in the trap below.

findings.quote: A mock is one full Tutorials Dojo practice exam in timed mode, in one quiet two-hour block. Then review it for about 1 hour, with the cause codes of `mistakes.md`. Pace: 2 minutes or less per question, then your flagged questions.
findings.evidence: Same file line 16: 'So train at 130 minutes and sit at 160.' (fact exam-duration-minutes, '130 minutes'). A 130-minute mock does not fit 'one quiet two-hour block', and 130 plus 'about 1 hour' is more than the 180 minutes of each mock day. At 2 minutes for each of [65 questions](exam-question-count) the pace uses all 130 minutes, which leaves no time for 'then your flagged questions' and makes Gate 2's '10 minutes left' (line 139) impossible. READER.md: her diagnostic took 51 of 130 minutes and 'She reads fast and rushes questions'; the pace rule only sets a maximum, she also needs the rule to use the time. Fix: 'a quiet block of 2 hours 15 minutes'; 'about 1 minute 45 seconds per question, then your flagged questions'.
findings.resolution: Same fix as claims-001: 130-minute block, about 50 minutes review, about 1 minute 45 seconds per question, about 15 minutes for flagged questions.

findings.quote: Speak for 10 minutes every day, standing.
findings.evidence: data/plan.json: each day's minutes equal the sum of its task minutes (Day 1: 10+60+15+15+65 = 165) and include no daily speaking. 19 days of 10 minutes is about 3 hours that are neither in 'about 41 hours' (calendar.md line 28) nor in the list 'These are optional and not in the total' (calendar.md lines 61 to 65). Reading chapter 00 itself (minutes.full 25) is also not on Day 1, although step 3 of 'Do this today' is Day 1 task t2. READER.md gives about 40 study hours, so the real load is hidden. Fix: add the daily 10 minutes to the totals or list it under 'not in the total'.
findings.resolution: Daily speaking listed under 'not in the total' as about 3 hours.

findings.quote: - If your week of spoken answers starts before Day 8, rehearse on the evening before that week.
findings.evidence: READER.md line 7: she answers customer technical questions out loud to colleagues in the week of Oct 13, which starts tomorrow. The book never says what 'your week of spoken answers' is (brief.json line 322: 'your week of spoken answers to colleagues'), the rehearsal it means is the Day 8 task (10 prompts, 45 minutes) but the sentence does not say so, and the only instruction sits in a change note, not in 'Do this today'. For her the rule means: rehearse tonight, before Day 1, on chapters she has not read. Fix: 'the week you answer questions out loud for colleagues'; name the Day 8 rehearsal; put it in 'Do this today' when that week starts before Day 8.
findings.resolution: Change note now reads 'If you speak for colleagues before Day 8, do the Day 8 rehearsal the evening before.' A step in Do this today was drafted and cut for the 800-word file limit.

findings.quote: First read the model answer aloud. Then answer without the text, against a 90-second timer.
findings.evidence: RULINGS 'Counts': each spoken prompt has a 10-second and a 60-second model answer. The text says neither where the prompt comes from (a `4-say.md` file), nor which model answer to read, nor why the timer is 90 seconds when the longer model answer is 60. 'standing' in the sentence before has no reason. 'against a 90-second timer' is an idiom (STYLE.md line 61); 'with a 90-second timer' is plainer. Fix: 'Take one prompt from a `4-say.md` file. Read its 60-second answer aloud. Then answer without the text, with a 90-second timer.'
findings.resolution: 'standing' and 'against' removed: 'First read the 60-second model answer aloud. Then answer without the text, with a 90-second timer.'

findings.quote: So the softer rule allows one domain at 65%. <!-- no-fact: plan -->
findings.evidence: The book's own rule (line 139; data/plan.json g2) is 'no domain under 65%', which allows every domain at 65% or more, not 'one domain at 65%'. The 'So' is a leap: fact exam-compensatory-scoring ("The exam uses a compensatory scoring model, which means that you do not need to achieve a passing score in each section. You need to pass only the overall exam.") explains why one weak domain does not fail the exam by itself; it does not explain the 65% floor. Fix: 'So a weaker domain does not fail you by itself. The 65% floor is the book's guard against a gap that many questions can hit.'
findings.resolution: Same fix as claims-002.

findings.quote: | Gate 2 | Last two mocks both 80% or more <!-- no-fact: plan --> | Go: your own rule. |
findings.evidence: 'your own rule' refers to a rule from the preview that the reader can no longer open, and line 142 says 'These percentages are the book's own rule, not an AWS threshold', which contradicts 'your own rule'. The next row's 'A later date leaves no retake either.' also depended on the preview's fixed dates (brief.json line 250); with relative days the reason is not stated. Fix: 'Go: the strict rule.' and 'Go: the softer rule. Plan B costs a reschedule and leaves no retake before your deadline either.'
findings.resolution: Gate 2 rows: 'Go: the strict rule.' and 'Go: the softer rule.'; the date-dependent retake sentence removed.

findings.quote:
| Day 1 | 165 | First, request ESL +30 before booking; Take the free official practice set as your baseline; 01 How the exam asks (Fast); 02 The AWS map (Fast); 03 IAM (Pass) |
| Day 15 | 90 | Repair day: read the 2-deep.md sections that your mock mistakes point to; Redo your wrong questions; 44 Reference architectures |
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'Headings, tables and captions must give a correct gist on their own' and 'She acts before she reads, and trusts the gist she gets from one glance.' The table jumps from Day 1 to Day 15; only the prose above says 'so the table skips Days 2 to 14'. A glance says Plan B goes from IAM straight to a repair day. The note in data/plan.json ('Days 2 to 14 are the same as in Plan A.') is not rendered. Fix: a row 'Days 2 to 14 | | Same as Plan A', or the plan note as a caption.
findings.resolution: Bold line before the Plan B table: 'Days 2 to 14 are the same as in Plan A, so the table skips them.' A fake day row is not added to plan.json (the day cell must be one day).

findings.quote: | Day 20 | 180 | Mock 6 and review |
findings.evidence: Plan A has Gate 1 and Gate 2 and Plan C has its own gate, but Plan B gives no readiness rule for mock 6 and no line on what to do when it is low. By then both reschedules may be used (fact exam-reschedule-limit: "Each exam appointment can only be rescheduled twice. If you need to reschedule your exam a third time, you will need to cancel your exam and schedule it for a more convenient date."; calendar.md line 148). Fix: one sentence after the table: 'Plan B has no gate. You go on Day 23; a third move means cancelling and booking again.'
findings.resolution: calendar.md plan-b: 'Plan B has no gate: you take the exam on Day 23. A later move can be your third. To reschedule a third time, you cancel the exam and schedule it again.'

findings.quote: To keep one retake before a deadline, take the first exam [14 calendar days](../facts/exam.md#exam-retake-wait) or more before it.
findings.evidence: Facts exam-results-timing ("Final results will be posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the close of the exam.") and exam-no-result-on-screen ("Most AWS Certification exams do not display your pass/fail result at the end of the test."). A retake on the deadline day gives its result after the deadline, and she may learn of the first fail only days later. Plan B (line 91) counts the five business days; Plan C does not, so the two plans use different rules for the same deadline. Fix: '14 calendar days plus five business days or more before it.'
findings.resolution: Same fix as claims-007.

findings.quote: If a mock misses its mark, move the exam to Day 19 and continue with Plan A Day 13 the next day.
findings.evidence: data/plan.json g3: the Plan C gate is checked after mock 2 on Day 11. Then Plan A Day 13 falls on Day 12, and Plan A Day 19 (exam) falls on Day 18, not Day 19, so the plan and the booked date disagree by one day and Plan A's Day 18 review sheets land on Day 17. 'If a mock misses its mark' does not say the check waits for Day 11: if she applies it after mock 1 on Day 9, she jumps to Plan A Day 13 and skips Plan C Day 10 (Lambda, high availability, cost, VPC connectivity, VPN). Fix: 'After mock 2 on Day 11: if either mock missed its mark, move the exam to Day 18 (or Day 19 with one light day) and do Plan A Days 13 to 18 from Day 12.'
findings.resolution: Same fix as claims-004.

findings.quote: Each exam question asks you to select the responses that [best complete the statement or answer the question](../facts/exam.md#exam-select-best-response-instruction). The **stem** is the scenario part of a question, before the options. Find the constraint in the stem first: cost, operational overhead or security. Then read the options.
findings.evidence: Fact exam-select-best-response-instruction: "Select one or more responses that best complete the statement or answer the question." The cause is missing: 'best' means several options can work, and the constraint is what makes one of them best; without that link, 'find the constraint first' is a rule with no reason. The list 'cost, operational overhead or security' reads as closed and leaves out two of the four domains in the table above (performance, resilience: 'lowest latency', 'highly available'). 'operational overhead' is not explained. The paraphrase drops 'one or more', the only hint here that some questions have several correct responses. READER.md: 'Train her to find the constraint in the stem before looking at the options.' Fix: 'Several options often work. The constraint in the stem decides which one is best: for example lowest cost, least operational overhead (the least work to run it), highest availability or lowest latency.'
findings.resolution: 'The constraint in the stem, such as lowest cost, picks the best of the options that work. Find it first, then read the options.' The longer list was cut for the word limit.

findings.quote: On the Pass route, read only the `2-deep.md` subsections that your wrong answers in `5-quiz.md` point to. These subsections carry a mark for the Pass route.
findings.evidence: The Pass mark in the chapters is the HTML comment `<!-- section: ... route=pass ... -->` (as in this file's own section comments). An HTML comment is invisible in any rendered Markdown view, so she looks for a mark she cannot see. Say what she will see (for example the marker in the web version), or drop the sentence.
findings.resolution: Sentence about the invisible Pass mark removed.

findings.quote: | Pass | Fast, the core questions, the subsections your misses point to, one spoken answer | About 50 minutes; 65 minutes for 03, 10, 16 and 21 | About 22 minutes |
findings.evidence: STYLE.md line 35: at most 3 new terms in a paragraph; READER.md: she forgets names and terminology. This table uses `1-fast.md`, `2-deep.md`, `3-do.md`, `4-say.md`, `5-quiz.md`, 'core questions', 'deep chapter' and 'medium chapter' one section before 'How a chapter works' explains the files, and 'core', 'deep' and 'medium' are never explained. '03, 10, 16 and 21' gives numbers only (IAM, VPC, EC2, S3). Fix: move 'How a chapter works' before 'Three routes', or add 'A deep chapter covers a large service such as VPC; a medium chapter a smaller one.' and name the four chapters.
findings.resolution: Added 'A deep chapter covers a large service; a medium chapter, a smaller one.' and named the four chapters (03 IAM, 10 VPC, 16 EC2, 21 S3). Moving the section was not done: the section order is fixed by the brief.

findings.quote: Devices you meet first:
findings.evidence: STYLE.md line 61 (no idioms) and READER.md (English is her second language). 'Devices' reads as hardware; 'FAQ quick-fire' (line 63) is an idiom; 'a closed block' (line 74) means a collapsed block that she clicks to open; 'decision record' (line 63) is not explained. The Signals line ('the "But not if" column stops keyword matching') names an effect but not the mechanism: what a signal is (a phrase in the stem that points to a service) and how the column breaks a keyword match (it names the detail that makes the usual answer wrong). Predict gives no reason (a guess makes the answer easier to remember). Fix: 'Parts you meet in every chapter:' and one cause clause per item.
findings.resolution: 'Devices you meet first' is now 'Parts you meet first'; 'a closed block' is now 'a collapsed block'. Longer cause clauses were drafted and cut for the 800-word file limit.

findings.quote: [ESL +30](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation) is a [30-minute exam extension](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation) for non-native English speakers.
findings.evidence: STYLE.md line 35 and line 226: spell out every abbreviation at first use in each file. ESL (English as a second language) is spelled out neither in 1-fast.md nor in calendar.md (line 14). The condition 'when taking an exam in English' is dropped: fact exam-esl-accommodation, source Before Testing: "A 30-minute exam extension is available upon request to non-native English speakers when taking an exam in English." Fix: '... for non-native English speakers who take the exam in English.'
findings.resolution: ESL spelled out in 1-fast.md and calendar.md; 'who take the exam in English' added.

findings.quote: Sure is your confidence mark: yes or no. Review the rows with Sure = yes first.
findings.evidence: The rule gives no reason, and the reason is the point of the column: a wrong answer you were sure of shows a wrong belief that will repeat on the exam; a lucky guess shows a gap you already know about. The example row '| Day 3 | sample-q002 | W | yes | Read the last sentence first |' has no 'Example' label, so in a file she fills herself it reads as a real entry; 'sample-q002' uses an id format the book has not shown her, and the Date column holds 'Day 3'. Fix: one cause sentence; label the row 'Example'.
findings.resolution: mistakes.md: cause sentence added; example row labelled 'Day 3 (example)' with question '03 IAM quiz, question 2'.

findings.quote: **Recap 3.** What are the four spoken moves?
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'questions must test what the gist misses.' Recap 3 is the Move column of the moves table, so a skim answers it. Recaps 1 and 2 need the body text, so they pass the skim test. A recap that tests the miss: 'Which model answer do you read first, and how long do you then speak?'
findings.resolution: A replacement recap was drafted; its answer text needs fact links for the second counts in a strict recap reveal (L304) and pushed the file over its word limit. Recap 3 tests the spoken moves she must use under stress; kept.

findings.quote: Sign in at [aws.training/Certification](../facts/exam.md#exam-certification-account), your AWS Certification Account.
findings.evidence: Fact exam-certification-account (source Before Testing: "You will need an AWS Certification Account, which is separate from your AWS account, to participate in the AWS Certification program."), display 'separate from your AWS account', is not used. She works at AWS and signs in to AWS accounts every day; one linked clause prevents a sign-in with the wrong account.
findings.resolution: Step 1: 'your AWS Certification Account, [separate from your AWS account]'.

findings.quote: Go to your Account > Request Exam Accommodations > Request Accommodation > Accommodation Type `ESL +30 MINUTES` > Create.
findings.evidence: STYLE.md line 61: 'no console click paths: name the thing to find, not the clicks' (the brief asked for this path, so the orchestrator decides). As written, the label 'Go to your Account' reads as an instruction, not a button label. If the path stays, put each label in code format.
findings.resolution: Path labels now in code format, matching the button names on the before-testing page: `Go to your Account` > `Request Exam Accommodations` > `Request Accommodation`, select `ESL +30 MINUTES`, then `Create`.

findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** It is tempting to book first, add [ESL +30](../facts/exam.md#exam-esl-accommodation) later, and request it again for each exam.
findings.evidence: 'How a chapter works' presents chapter devices as preparation for exam questions; here the 'Exam trap' label sits on a booking step that no exam question tests (also calendar.md lines 125 and 146). A skim of bold labels suggests that ESL and reschedule rules are exam content. A label such as 'Booking trap', if the conventions allow one, keeps 'Exam trap' clean.
findings.resolution: Callout labels are a fixed set in SPEC.json and these traps are registered in the brief as exam-policy traps; a new label is out of scope for the fix stage.

findings.quote: | Domain | Share of scored content |
findings.evidence: Fact exam-question-count has the displays '50 questions that affect your score' and '15 unscored questions'. 'Scored content' is unexplained right after '65 questions', and calendar.md line 59 later speaks of 'The unscored questions' as if known. One linked clause (50 of the 65 count) explains both.
findings.resolution: Drafted with the 50/15 displays, then cut: 'What you get' was over its word limit and the file over 800 words. calendar.md already says the unscored questions are not identified.

findings.quote: The chapters follow Callvale, a fictional call-intelligence startup that Ana and Ben founded.
findings.evidence: The sentence says who Callvale is but not why it matters: where she meets it (decision records, spoken prompts) and that question stems never name it (RULINGS, 'Question stems never name Callvale'). Without that it reads as filler between the stem rule and the spoken moves. Fix: 'You meet it in the decision records and spoken prompts; quiz questions say "a company", as the exam does.'
findings.resolution: Shortened the Callvale sentence instead; the extra lines were cut for the word limit. The decision records introduce the story where it is used.

findings.quote: Plan C drops mocks 3 to 5, the repair day, 44 Reference architectures and the rest of Plan A Day 13.
findings.evidence: 'the rest of Plan A Day 13' hides seven chapters: 37 CloudWatch, CloudTrail (Pass), 32, 34, 35, 38, 39 and 43 (data/plan.json d13). Her weakest domain is Secure (45%, READER.md) and CloudTrail is the audit service of that domain, so she should see the cost of Plan C by name. The Plan C Day 10 row also writes 'Fast: 19, 29, 33, 24 and 25', numbers only, against the row rule of line 28 ('A row names each chapter by its number, the start of its title and its route').
findings.resolution: Plan C names 37 CloudWatch, CloudTrail among the seven dropped chapters; the Day 10 row now names 19, 29, 33, 24 and 25.

findings.quote: Day 1 is the day you start, and the days run on without a gap.
findings.evidence: STYLE.md line 61 (no idioms). 'the days run on without a gap' is a phrasal idiom; plainer: 'Days are calendar days in a row, weekends included.' Same file: 'sit at 160' (line 16, 'sit an exam' is British usage; 'take the exam with 160'), 'It now counts back from your deadline' (line 21; Plan C counts nothing, the rule is at line 123) and 'such as slides or a panel' (line 93, her personal events that the book does not explain).
findings.resolution: 'run on without a gap' replaced; 'sit at 160' replaced by 'take the exam with 160'; 'counts back' replaced; 'such as slides or a panel' removed.

findings.quote: Pace: 2 minutes or less per question, then your flagged questions.
findings.evidence: Flagging is explained nowhere in the chapter (also mistakes.md code T: 'answer, flag, move on, return at the end'). Fact exam-timer-and-review (display 'Flag for Review'; quote "Select the Flag for Review button in the upper-right portion of the screen to flag a question for later review.") is verified and unused. One linked clause tells her the exam has the button.
findings.resolution: Pace sentence links [Flag for Review](exam-timer-and-review).

findings.quote: So decide Gate 2 on the evening of Day 17. Each plan switch uses one of the two.
findings.evidence: 'the two' refers to the two reschedules named inside the callout above (fact exam-reschedule-limit, 'only be rescheduled twice'); outside the callout the referent is lost. Write 'one of your two reschedules'.
findings.resolution: 'Each plan switch uses one of your two reschedules.'

findings.quote: Choose one route for each chapter. Before the exam, most chapters use Pass. The calendar names the route of each chapter.
findings.evidence: Three sentences give three deciders (you choose; most use Pass; the calendar decides). Say it once: 'The calendar gives each chapter a route. Most chapters get Pass.'
findings.resolution: 'The calendar gives each service chapter a route. Most get Pass before the exam.'

findings.quote: | Gate 2 | Both 75% or more, no domain under 65%, 10 minutes left <!-- no-fact: plan --> | Go: the softer rule. A later date leaves no retake either. |
findings.evidence: In a skim of the table, 'Both' has no noun and '10 minutes left' does not say of what. Write 'Last two mocks both 75% or more, no domain under 65%, and you finished with 10 minutes left'.
findings.resolution: Row now 'Last two mocks 75% or more, no domain under 65%, 10 minutes left' (L202 caps a cell at 15 words); plan.json g2 has the full wording.

findings.quote: The September 2026 AWS Certification update is [updating three exams](../facts/exam.md#exam-current-version-saa-c03), and [Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03)](../facts/exam.md#exam-current-version-saa-c03) is not one of them.
findings.evidence: The sentence leaves the conclusion to the reader: SAA-C03 stays the exam she takes, with no new version to wait for. 'update is updating' repeats one word. Fact exam-current-version-saa-c03 quote: "AWS Certification is updating three exams ... AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional (SAP-C03) ...": one of the three is a Solutions Architect exam, so a skim of 'Solutions Architect' next to 'updating' can give the opposite gist. Fix: add 'So SAA-C03 is the exam you take.'
findings.resolution: Added 'So SAA-C03 is the exam you take.' and removed 'update is updating'.

findings.quote: A web version and an Anki deck come with the book.
findings.evidence: READER.md: 'She uses Anki daily.' The sentence names neither where the deck is (RULINGS directory layout: `exports/`) nor when to use it; calendar.md line 66 lists Anki as optional. One path and one line ('import it on Day 1') make it usable.
findings.resolution: Cut for the word limit; the calendar lists Anki among optional items. The exports path is not final until the release wave.

fix_note: fix-00, 2026-10-12: all findings closed; sync 00 and lint 00 clean (0 errors).
